scope: Unit author hypotheses at corrected submission; independent review required

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces review needs the exact component set and policy version for one attempted catalog change, and rejection must preserve the catalog.
items.decisiveFact: Review needs the exact component set and policy version for one attempted catalog change, and rejection must preserve the catalog.
items.nearestAlternative: A direct catalog method is simpler for an immediate change, but it does not retain the reviewed proposal when the request is delayed or rejected.
items.changedCondition: If no proposal history or deferred review existed, a direct method call could be enough.
items.identityReason: The current key selects a command object for identifiable, reviewable work. This version keeps the bundle-change domain and makes the proposal snapshot the specific reason for that object.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces a retry of the same reservation intent must refer to the original outcome and must not consume capacity twice.
items.decisiveFact: A retry of the same reservation intent must refer to the original outcome and must not consume capacity twice.
items.nearestAlternative: Calling reserve again with the same values seems sufficient, but equal values do not distinguish a retry from a separate reservation request.
items.changedCondition: If the client could never retry after an uncertain response, direct invocation might be sufficient.
items.identityReason: The current key's command concept is retained and the charger-reservation facts now specify why a request needs operation identity across a retry.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces the change needs before-and-after metadata history, while undo must preserve the existing asset identity.
items.decisiveFact: The change needs before-and-after metadata history, while undo must preserve the existing asset identity.
items.nearestAlternative: Storing a whole replacement asset is convenient, but restoration must change descriptive values without substituting a new asset identity.
items.changedCondition: If the merge were permanent and had no review or undo requirement, direct metadata mutation could be sufficient.
items.identityReason: The existing item tests identifiable operations. This retains the metadata-merge use case and makes the reversible change—not generic command vocabulary—the distinguishing decision.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces execution needs the requested territory and expiry, plus an authorization check against the executing analyst, with attributable result data.
items.decisiveFact: Execution needs the requested territory and expiry, plus an authorization check against the executing analyst, with attributable result data.
items.nearestAlternative: A queue of callbacks can execute the work later, but it hides the operation's requested scope and makes its audit data depend on callback code.
items.changedCondition: If approval were immediate and no attribution or queueing were required, a direct service call might suffice.
items.identityReason: This keeps the command-object decision but specializes it to queued rights approval with execution-time authorization and captured scope.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces undo is conditional on the battery's current assignment matching the assignment captured by the approved replacement.
items.decisiveFact: Undo is conditional on the battery's current assignment matching the assignment captured by the approved replacement.
items.nearestAlternative: A log that stores only the battery ID is smaller, but cannot determine which aircraft association the undo is allowed to reverse.
items.changedCondition: If assignment were immutable after approval, a simple prior-value log could suffice.
items.identityReason: The source item already concerns scheduling a battery replacement. This makes the conditional reversible operation specific without changing its core command decision.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces the delayed route is bound to one approved recipient and must be rejected if consent is withdrawn before execution.
items.decisiveFact: The delayed route is bound to one approved recipient and must be rejected if consent is withdrawn before execution.
items.nearestAlternative: A queued callback can read the current recipient later, but it could route to a different destination than the patient approved.
items.changedCondition: If routing were immediate and consent could not change between approval and action, a direct call could suffice.
items.identityReason: This retains the referral and consent boundary from the source but changes the learner decision from generic privacy ownership to a captured, revocable pending operation.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces the attempt is evaluated against the revision and scoring policy captured at its start, not the later current defaults.
items.decisiveFact: The attempt is evaluated against the revision and scoring policy captured at its start, not the later current defaults.
items.nearestAlternative: A completion callback can look up the latest exercise, but that can grade an attempt under rules the learner never used.
items.changedCondition: If attempts always completed synchronously before a revision could change, a direct call using current values might be adequate.
items.identityReason: The original music-practice case and recorded revision/policy are retained; the candidate makes the delayed completion's captured inputs the decision under test.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces the approval is attributable and bounded by controls; a rejected control leaves the request pending rather than partially approved.
items.decisiveFact: The approval is attributable and bounded by controls; a rejected control leaves the request pending rather than partially approved.
items.nearestAlternative: A queue of manager IDs is smaller, but it loses the rationale and control scope that define the requested exception.
items.changedCondition: If approval were immediate and no review history or rejection behavior existed, a direct service operation might be enough.
items.identityReason: The source approval case and bounded-control meaning remain; the candidate makes an attributable queued operation and its rejection result explicit.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces review compares a proposed source-to-segment mapping, while rejection leaves the current recording unchanged.
items.decisiveFact: Review compares a proposed source-to-segment mapping, while rejection leaves the current recording unchanged.
items.nearestAlternative: Replacing the recording in place is direct, but it would change the asset before the mapping review accepts the proposal.
items.changedCondition: If the source had no annotations or review stage, a direct replacement could be simpler.
items.identityReason: The source podcast replacement and stable-annotation invariant are retained, with the candidate making the proposed mapping/rejection decision concrete.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces one approval-scoped grant has a fixed expiry and retries must not create another active grant for that same approval.
items.decisiveFact: One approval-scoped grant has a fixed expiry and retries must not create another active grant for that same approval.
items.nearestAlternative: A worker can resolve the latest approval when it runs, but that may bind the grant to a different approval than the queued request.
items.changedCondition: If role grant were synchronous and had no retry or expiry data, a direct call might suffice.
items.identityReason: The source temporary-role case remains, and the candidate makes the approval-scoped, retryable grant intent explicit.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces the seal is bound to an exact revision and execution must reject if that revision is no longer current.
items.decisiveFact: The seal is bound to an exact revision and execution must reject if that revision is no longer current.
items.nearestAlternative: A queue containing only the document ID can fetch the latest revision, but then it can seal a revision the notary did not inspect.
items.changedCondition: If sealing were immediate and the document revision could not change during the call, a direct method could suffice.
items.identityReason: The source notary-seal use case and exact-revision invariant remain, now focused on delayed execution against the revision the notary approved.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces release is order-scoped and retries reuse the same payout result, while another order needs a distinct identity.
items.decisiveFact: Release is order-scoped and retries reuse the same payout result, while another order needs a distinct identity.
items.nearestAlternative: A seller ID can find outstanding orders, but it does not specify which settled order this release request means.
items.changedCondition: If each order could be released only once synchronously with no retry, a direct operation might suffice.
items.identityReason: The source seller-payout case is preserved; the candidate makes the settled-order scope and same-request result the command identity decision.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces the scenario explicitly requires sequence-ordered application and no state change when a sequence is rejected.
items.decisiveFact: The scenario explicitly requires sequence-ordered application and no state change when a sequence is rejected.
items.nearestAlternative: A notification stream can publish updates, but delivery order alone is not the required effective sequence and may not match it.
items.changedCondition: If announcements had no required effective ordering and displays could simply show the latest value, a plain current-platform update could suffice.
items.identityReason: The source transit scenario's effective-order promise remains, with the explicit sequence protocol made part of the operation rather than inferred from notification order.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces the overlap rule applies to a specific meter and interval, and review rejection must preserve existing reservations.
items.decisiveFact: The overlap rule applies to a specific meter and interval, and review rejection must preserve existing reservations.
items.nearestAlternative: A queue of meter IDs can recheck current windows, but it no longer represents the interval the operator asked to reserve.
items.changedCondition: If the reservation were immediate and no review could delay it, a direct request might suffice.
items.identityReason: The source energy-sharing case and overlap invariant are retained; the candidate makes the exact reviewed interval the operation identity.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces the two assignment changes form one all-or-nothing request whose validation covers both new placements.
items.decisiveFact: The two assignment changes form one all-or-nothing request whose validation covers both new placements.
items.nearestAlternative: Two independent assignment updates can each validate their own new shift, but the first could succeed before the second fails.
items.changedCondition: If each move were independent and partial completion were allowed, separate assignment operations could be acceptable.
items.identityReason: The source two-volunteer swap and qualifications invariant remain; this version focuses the decision on representing one paired intent rather than two unrelated writes.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces the offline change is based on a specific revision, and a stale base must produce a conflict without overwriting current geometry.
items.decisiveFact: The offline change is based on a specific revision, and a stale base must produce a conflict without overwriting current geometry.
items.nearestAlternative: A callback that merges into the latest geometry is convenient, but it cannot detect whether the user's base revision is stale.
items.changedCondition: If no concurrent edits were possible, merging directly into the sole current revision might be sufficient.
items.identityReason: The source offline-route use case and no-silent-overwrite invariant remain; this candidate makes the named base revision the operation's decisive input.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces the operation targets a chosen character/reward and must validate campaign phase before changing either target or campaign state.
items.decisiveFact: The operation targets a chosen character/reward and must validate campaign phase before changing either target or campaign state.
items.nearestAlternative: A UI button can be hidden outside the reward phase, but a direct request still needs the same check before it mutates the character.
items.changedCondition: If rewards were always legal and applied synchronously without attribution, direct mutation could be adequate.
items.identityReason: The source campaign-reward context is retained; the candidate focuses on a reviewable operation carrying its targets and phase prerequisite.

items.learningObjective: Choose a design that enforces the shipment changes ownership only after the replacement carrier accepts while retaining its temperature restrictions.
items.decisiveFact: The shipment changes ownership only after the replacement carrier accepts while retaining its temperature restrictions.
items.nearestAlternative: A direct owner-field update is simple, but it can make the new carrier current before the hand-off is accepted.
items.changedCondition: If no hand-off acceptance step existed, changing the owner field after validation could be enough.
items.identityReason: The source cold-chain and carrier-reassignment case is retained; the candidate sharpens its operation identity around the acceptance boundary and preserved restrictions.
